title: Peace with God
definition: Peace with God is the reconciled standing believers have through justification by faith in Jesus Christ.
summary: Peace with God is the settled condition of acceptance and reconciliation secured by justification in Christ.
christFocus: Jesus Christ makes peace through His blood and brings believers into restored fellowship with God.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Peace with God is the reconciled standing believers have because of justification through Christ. Scripture teaches that sinners are not naturally neutral toward God, but need peace made by grace.

This peace is deeper than calm feelings. It means the conflict caused by sin has been answered at the cross and the believer is no longer under condemnation.

Jesus made peace by the blood of His cross. The believer's assurance rests not in changing emotions but in the finished work of the Prince of Peace.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Peace with God matters because troubled consciences often mistake emotional unrest for rejection by God. This doctrine shows that peace is secured by Christ before it is felt steadily in the heart.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: When guilt or fear rises, return to the truth of Romans 5:1. Pray from your reconciled position, pursue peace with others, and help anxious believers distinguish peace with God from temporary emotional struggle.
